figures.caption: Fig. 1. Representation of the degradation mechanisms effect on the voltage curve of LFP cells (based on [17]), a) cell in a fresh state, b) effect of loss of lithium inventory, c) effect of loss of active material in the positive electrode in delithiated state, d) effect of loss of active material in the positive electrode in lithiated state, e) effect of loss of active material in the negative electrode in delithiated state, f) effect of loss of active material in the negative electrode in lithiated state.
Fig. 2. Novel structure of BMS for degradation mechanisms and actual battery capacity determination.
Fig. 3. Working principle of the “not real-time” calculation block.

Fig. 4. Correlation between the plateaus’ lengths in the considered standard condition and the corresponding length under speciﬁed condition for differently aged cells for the charge process, a) correlation between the length of plateau IIA for a current rate of 0.1C and the length of the same plateau for a different current rate, b) correlation between the length of plateau IA for an ambient temperature of 23 C and the length of the same plateau for a different ambient temperature.

Fig. 5. Online detection of the plateaus during driving phase at 23 C, a) current proﬁle of a repeated FTP75 driving cycle, b) comparison among the ofﬂine measured OCV and quasi-OCV curve and the tracked and ﬁltered OCV values by means of an equivalent electrical circuit model.

Fig. 6. Example of the evolution of the parameters during the ofﬂine aging estimation, a) evolution of the LLI, b) evolution of the LAM on the negative electrode in the deli- thiated phase, c) evolution of the total error, d) evolution of the error related to the single plateaus, where L1/VA and L3/IA.
Fig. 7. Results of the ofﬂine estimation of the total capacity for the different considered scenarios, a) for the charge process and b) for the discharge process.

Fig. 8. Recalibration of OCV hysteresis model by means of tracked degradation modes, a) OCV hysteresis measured for a fresh (blue circles and dotted lines) and for an aged cell (red lozenges and continuous lines) during charge and discharge, b) OCV hysteresis of the aged cell (red lozenges and continuous lines) and hysteresis of the new cell (green squares and dotted lines) after recalibration, c) error between OCV of a fresh and aged cell, d) error between OCV of an aged and a fresh cell after recalibration. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this ﬁgure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)
